Under the **protocol 2.0 / SAP v2.0** rule (EP-A-WT24.R2, ±14-day analysis window, Amendment 1), the mean percent change in body weight from baseline to Week 24 in the **FAS population** for data through 2026-10-31 is: [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-e14628c5-7a89-40dd-9447-1fbaad365514)

| Arm | FAS (N) | Derived (n) | Mean % Change |
|-----|---------|-------------|---------------|
| **CSL101** (CSL-101 10 mg QW) | 2,772 | 2,410 | **−12.66%** |
| **PBO** (Placebo) | 1,271 | 1,115 | **−2.30%** |

### Key details

- **Rule version**: EP-A-WT24.R2 — the ±14-day Week 24 window introduced by Amendment 1 (protocol 2.0 / SAP 2.0). [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-8cf7d79a-9162-4dd7-95b2-1cd395a59ccf)
- **Population**: Full Analysis Set (FAS — randomized and dosed); mean is computed over participants with a derived endpoint only. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-f0e6805a-69a8-4a0c-a932-d3505bae2733)
- **Missingness**: ~13.1% (CSL101) and ~12.3% (PBO) of FAS participants had no derived endpoint (no imputation). [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/1e4c20d426df40f38b084a533ca1e830?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_007c1f)
- **Data cutoff**: All FAS participants' Week 24 target dates fall on or before 2026-10-31, so the full dataset is included in this cut. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/1e4c20d426df40f38b084a533ca1e830?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_oujFcY)
- Negative values indicate weight loss. Results are **descriptive only** (synthetic data; not evidence of efficacy). [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-cf3beb25-95e9-4acd-a91b-6de48daad2a7)

ORDER BY `Arm`

snippets.headline: Mean percent change summarizes unrounded body-weight change among FAS participants with derived results, where negative values indicate weight loss.

wins).

genie_one_sql:
SELECT VSTESTCD, VSSTRESU, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(VSSTRESN) AS min_val, MAX(VSSTRESN) AS max_val
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`silver_vs`
WHERE `STUDYID` = 'CSL-A' AND `VSTESTCD` = 'HEIGHT'
GROUP BY `VSTESTCD`, `VSSTRESU`

SELECT MIN(`reference_date`) AS min_ref, MAX(`reference_date`) AS max_ref,
       MIN(`followup_target_date`) AS min_fu_target, MAX(`followup_target_date`) AS max_fu_target
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`gold_endpoint_result`
WHERE `STUDYID` = 'CSL-A' AND `endpoint_version` = 'EP-A-WT24.R2'

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT `USUBJID`) AS participants_with_height,
       COUNT(*) AS total_height_records,
       ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT `USUBJID`), 2) AS records_per_participant
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`silver_vs`
WHERE `STUDYID` = 'CSL-A' AND `VSTESTCD` = 'HEIGHT'

SELECT MAX(vs.`VSDTC`) AS max_followup_obs_date
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`gold_endpoint_result` er
JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`silver_vs` vs
  ON er.`followup_observation_id` = vs.`CPL_OBS_ID`
WHERE er.`STUDYID` = 'CSL-A' AND er.`endpoint_version` = 'EP-A-WT24.R2'
  AND er.`result_status` = 'DERIVED'

WITH height AS (
  SELECT `USUBJID`, `VSSTRESN` AS height_cm
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`silver_vs`
  WHERE `STUDYID` = 'CSL-A' AND `VSTESTCD` = 'HEIGHT'
),
endpoint AS (
  SELECT er.`USUBJID`,
         pp.`ARMCD`,
         er.`BASE`,
         er.`PCHG`,
         er.`result_status`,
         er.`analysis_population_status`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`gold_endpoint_result` er
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`gold_participant_population` pp
    ON er.`USUBJID` = pp.`USUBJID`
  WHERE er.`STUDYID` = 'CSL-A'
    AND er.`endpoint_version` = 'EP-A-WT24.R2'
    AND er.`analysis_population_status` = 'IN_FAS'
    AND er.`result_status` = 'DERIVED'
)
SELECT e.`ARMCD` AS arm,
       COUNT(*) AS n_participants,
       ROUND(AVG(e.`PCHG`), 2) AS mean_pct_change,
       ROUND(AVG(e.`BASE` / POWER(h.`height_cm` / 100.0, 2)), 1) AS mean_baseline_bmi
FROM endpoint e
JOIN height h ON e.`USUBJID` = h.`USUBJID`
WHERE (e.`BASE` / POWER(h.`height_cm` / 100.0, 2)) >= 35
GROUP BY e.`ARMCD`
ORDER BY e.`ARMCD`

SELECT pp.`ARMCD` AS arm,
       COUNT(*) AS n_fas_derived
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`gold_endpoint_result` er
JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`gold_participant_population` pp
  ON er.`USUBJID` = pp.`USUBJID`
WHERE er.`STUDYID` = 'CSL-A'
  AND er.`endpoint_version` = 'EP-A-WT24.R2'
  AND er.`analysis_population_status` = 'IN_FAS'
  AND er.`result_status` = 'DERIVED'
GROUP BY pp.`ARMCD`
ORDER BY pp.`ARMCD`

snippets.headline: Weight-related comorbidity membership requires descent from an included class root and excludes descendants of any exclusion root, with exclusions winning.
snippets.content: WRC-V1 means weight-related comorbidity, also labeled 'comorbidity class'. For eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.mondo_closure, INCLUDE `ancestor_code IN (SELECT concept_id FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.class_root WHERE class_id = 'WRC-V1' AND kind = 'root')` AND EXCLUDE `descendant_code IN (SELECT x.descendant_code FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.mondo_closure x JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.class_root r ON x.ancestor_code = r.concept_id WHERE r.class_id = 'WRC-V1' AND r.kind = 'exclude_root')`. Exclusion wins even when an inclusion root is reached. WRC-V2 extends WRC-V1 and inherits roots. For a disease membership question, restrict `descendant_code` to its concept and return `CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END`; examples map familial hypercholesterolemia to 'MONDO:0005439' and obstructive sleep apnea to 'MONDO:0007147'. The ancestry explanation query selects `c.ancestor_code AS class_root, c.ancestor_name, c.depth`, joins roots on `r.concept_id = c.ancestor_code AND r.kind = 'root' AND r.class_id = 'WRC-V1'`, and uses `NOT EXISTS` over exclusion-root ancestry for the same descendant.

snippets.headline: Amendment 1 widened CSL-A’s Week 24 analysis window to fourteen days effective September first, 2025.
snippets.content: For CSL-A, protocol 2.0 is Amendment 1 and became effective on `2025-09-01`. That amendment widened the Week 24 analysis window to ±14 days. The study-version history is stored in `eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.study_version`.

snippets.headline: The clinical study lab uses synthetic standards-linked study data, with fictional studies and descriptive results rather than submission-ready evidence.
snippets.content: Clinical Study Lab — Standards & Semantics covers synthetic Clinical Study Context & Evidence Lab data. CSL-101 is a fictional GLP-1 receptor agonist, and CSL-A and CSL-B are fictional studies. Data are SDTM-/ADaM-shaped, not submission-ready, and results are descriptive rather than evidence of efficacy, superiority, or causal effects. The standards domain covers MONDO diseases, MED-RT classes, mechanisms, physiologic effects and contraindications, MeSH bridging MED-RT conditions to MONDO, RxNorm ingredients, CDISC Controlled Terminology, and COSMoS concepts and dataset specializations. HEDIS, health-plan, NCQA and care-gap data are outside this space; MedDRA, SNOMED CT, ATC and the CDISC Library are not used.

Physical body-weight observations, also called 'weight records', INCLUDE rows from eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.silver_vs where `VSTESTCD = 'WEIGHT'`. snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: SSD addresses diabetes screening for patients with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder on antipsychotics. Its source is eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ssd_compliance_metrics. This is a serious mental illness population, not the diabetes cohort; its denominator is not compared with other measures' denominators.

snippets.headline: Diabetes eligibility follows diagnosis descendants under three ICD categories, while screening for antipsychotic users uses a different clinical cohort.
snippets.content: The diabetes cohort is defined by subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy under E10, E11, and E13, rather than only exact matches to those three codes. SSD means Diabetes Screening for People on Antipsychotics and uses a separate cohort: serious mental illness plus antipsychotic dispensing, ages 18–64. Its numerator is a glucose or HbA1c screen, not diabetes-cohort membership. SSD patient-level screening gaps INCLUDE rows in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ssd where evidence_datetime IS NULL.

snippets.headline: Qualifying complications include diabetes kidney, eye, and other specified complication descendants under nine explicitly listed ancestor codes.
snippets.content: A patient is classified as having a qualifying complication when `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition` contains an `icd10_code` whose closure match in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure` has `ancestor_code IN ('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2','E11.3','E10.3','E13.3','E11.4','E10.4','E13.4')`. The full included ancestor-code list is exactly `('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2','E11.3','E10.3','E13.3','E11.4','E10.4','E13.4')`; no other ancestor codes are included by this rule. The complication cohort is deduplicated with `SELECT DISTINCT c.patient_id` before it is used in the clinic metric.

snippets.headline: High A1c evidence counts distinguish all qualifying records from observation-backed records and records also linked to protocol triggers.
snippets.content: High A1c evidence coverage uses `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd g` with `g.evidence_value > 9.0`, INNER JOINed by `patient_id` to a one-row-per-patient rollup from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` restricted to `icd10_code LIKE 'E1%'`; the rollup calculates `MIN(icd10_code) FILTER (WHERE onset_date <= DATE'2026-12-31') AS prim`, but does not require `prim` to be non-null. Observation support is a correlated `count(*)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation o` where `o.patient_id = g.patient_id AND o.result_ts = g.evidence_datetime AND o.value_num = g.evidence_value`, producing `matches`. Protocol-trigger support is a correlated `count(*)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_protocol_adherence p` where `p.patient_id = g.patient_id AND p.trigger_ts = g.evidence_datetime`, producing `is_trigger`; no direct observation-to-protocol join is used. The jointly reported measures are `count(*) poor`, `count_if(matches > 0) observed`, and `count_if(matches > 0 AND is_trigger > 0) observed_trigger`, all at the retained adherence-row grain, not distinct-patient grain. Multiple observation or protocol matches do not multiply adherence rows because they are counted in scalar subqueries; replacing these with raw joins would risk fanout. Unlike the eligible status population, this population has no `measurement_year` or `eligible_flag` restriction and includes the broader diagnosis pattern `'E1%'`.

snippets.content: The exposed `Arm` dimension is sourced from `ARMCD` and has exactly these documented values: `CSL101` = CSL-101 10 mg once weekly and `PBO` = placebo. Include both arms with `Arm IN ('CSL101', 'PBO')` for a randomized treatment-versus-placebo comparison, or filter to one value for an arm-specific result. This particular supplied filter contains only the root-inclusion condition.

snippets.headline: Participants compared counts randomized CSL-A participants evaluated under both endpoint rule versions.
snippets.content: `Participants Compared` is the named measure for the number of randomized CSL-A participants compared across R1 and R2, with definition-time expression `COUNT(1)` over the metric view source. Query it as `MEASURE(`Participants Compared`)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study_semantic`.`amendment_impact_metrics`; do not select the measure bare or replace it with `COUNT`, `SUM`, or another aggregate over the metric view. Example: `SELECT `Arm`, MEASURE(`Participants Compared`) AS `participants_compared` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study_semantic`.`amendment_impact_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.content: Enrolled in error, also called 'eligibility violations', includes reconciliation = 'ENROLLED_BUT_RULE_INELIGIBLE' in eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.gold_participant_population. The measure is COUNT_IF(gold_participant_population.reconciliation = 'ENROLLED_BUT_RULE_INELIGIBLE'). The study-specific inclusion filters are STUDYID = 'CSL-A' and STUDYID = 'CSL-B', respectively. The semantic report uses eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_semantic.participant_population_metrics grouped by `Study`, with MEASURE(`Enrolled In Error`) and MEASURE(`Randomized Participants`), ordered by `Study`. No underlying randomized-participant formula is supplied.

snippets.headline: Study identifiers distinguish the 72-week obesity study from the 52-week type 2 diabetes study.

A participant with BMI ≥ 27 and < 30 qualifies for CSL-A only with at least one member of this class.

**Roots (WRC-V1):** hypertensive disorder (MONDO:0005044), hyperlipidemia (MONDO:0021187), hypertriglyceridemia
(MONDO:0005347), type 2 diabetes mellitus (MONDO:0005148), prediabetes syndrome (MONDO:0006920), coronary artery
disorder (MONDO:0005010), heart failure (MONDO:0005252), stroke disorder (MONDO:0005098), peripheral arterial
disease (MONDO:0005386), MASLD (MONDO:0013209).

**Carve-outs (exclusion wins):** pulmonary hypertension (MONDO:0005149), pregnancy-induced hypertension
(MONDO:0024664), congenital coronary artery malformation (MONDO:0015203).

**WRC-V2 (Amendment 1, protocol 2.0)** = WRC-V1 + obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (MONDO:0007147). Central sleep apnea is not
added.

**Membership** is the root and everything under it by is_a, at any depth, minus anything under a carve-out. MONDO
is a polyhierarchy, so a term can reach a root through one parent and a carve-out through another (then it is not a
member). The class is **not** a flat list of codes.

## 3,123 Randomized CSL-A Participants Have ≥ 1 Weight-Related Comorbidity (WRC-V1)

Of the **4,055** randomized CSL-A participants through 2026-10-31, **3,123 (77.0%)** have at least one weight-related comorbidity in their medical history, as defined by the protocol 1.0 / section 5.1 comorbidity class **WRC-V1**. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/e10d8af4ea0642f0a615a5eb9839644f?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_db4d89) [Weight-related comorbidity class (WRC-V1 / WRC-V2)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/ef6ec006-308e-475e-8bb5-ba22778d76cd?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### WRC-V1 Definition (Protocol 1.0)

WRC-V1 membership is determined by MONDO ontology subsumption — a condition qualifies if it is a descendant of any WRC-V1 root and **not** a descendant of any carve-out (exclusion wins). [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-89a7dc7e-06b2-4ee4-b025-62f6045be5e0)

The 10 root conditions and three carve-outs (pulmonary hypertension, pregnancy-induced hypertension, congenital coronary artery malformation) are the original protocol 1.0 set — **before** Amendment 1 (protocol 2.0) added obstructive sleep apnea as WRC-V2. [Protocol amendments (CSL-A)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/49392558-5839-44cb-ad4d-15acd5ff5d4c?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### Breakdown by Comorbidity Root

<!-- begin-embedded:query_aac568 -->
| comorbidity_root | participants |
| --- | --- |
| hypertensive disorder | 1352 |
| hyperlipidemia | 927 |
| type 2 diabetes mellitus | 504 |
| prediabetes syndrome | 502 |
| metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease | 254 |
| hypertriglyceridemia | 227 |
| coronary artery disorder | 173 |
| heart failure | 85 |
| stroke disorder | 41 |
| peripheral arterial disease | 37 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_aac568 -->

**Hypertensive disorder** is the most prevalent root, present in 1,352 participants, followed by **hyperlipidemia** (927) and **type 2 diabetes / prediabetes** (\~500 each). [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/e10d8af4ea0642f0a615a5eb9839644f?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_aac568) Note that participants can map to multiple roots, so the root-level counts sum to more than 3,123.
genie_one_sql:
WITH wrc_v1_members AS (
  -- All MONDO codes that are members of WRC-V1 (descendants of roots, minus descendants of exclude_roots)
  SELECT DISTINCT mc.descendant_code
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.mondo_closure mc
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.class_root r
    ON mc.ancestor_code = r.concept_id
   AND r.class_id = 'WRC-V1'
   AND r.kind = 'root'
  WHERE mc.descendant_code NOT IN (
    SELECT x.descendant_code
    FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.mondo_closure x
    JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.class_root e
      ON x.ancestor_code = e.concept_id
     AND e.class_id = 'WRC-V1'
     AND e.kind = 'exclude_root'
  )
),
randomized_csla AS (
  -- Randomized CSL-A participants through 2026-10-31
  SELECT p.USUBJID
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.gold_participant_population p
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.silver_dm dm
    ON p.USUBJID = dm.USUBJID AND p.STUDYID = dm.STUDYID
  WHERE p.STUDYID = 'CSL-A'
    AND p.randomized = true
    AND dm.CPL_RANDDT <= '2026-10-31'
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.USUBJID) AS participants_with_wrc_v1_comorbidity,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM randomized_csla) AS total_randomized_csla
FROM randomized_csla r
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.silver_mh mh
  ON r.USUBJID = mh.USUBJID
JOIN wrc_v1_members w
  ON mh.CPL_MONDO_ID = w.descendant_code

WITH randomized_csla AS (
  SELECT p.USUBJID
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.gold_participant_population p
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.silver_dm dm
    ON p.USUBJID = dm.USUBJID AND p.STUDYID = dm.STUDYID
  WHERE p.STUDYID = 'CSL-A'
    AND p.randomized = true
    AND dm.CPL_RANDDT <= '2026-10-31'
),
wrc_v1_excluded AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT x.descendant_code
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.mondo_closure x
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.class_root e
    ON x.ancestor_code = e.concept_id
   AND e.class_id = 'WRC-V1'
   AND e.kind = 'exclude_root'
),
mh_with_root AS (
  -- For each MH record of a randomized CSL-A participant, find which WRC-V1 root(s) it maps to
  SELECT DISTINCT
    r.USUBJID,
    cr.concept_id AS root_concept_id,
    mc_root.ancestor_name AS comorbidity_root
  FROM randomized_csla r
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.silver_mh mh
    ON r.USUBJID = mh.USUBJID
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.mondo_closure mc
    ON mh.CPL_MONDO_ID = mc.descendant_code
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.class_root cr
    ON mc.ancestor_code = cr.concept_id
   AND cr.class_id = 'WRC-V1'
   AND cr.kind = 'root'
  -- Get the root's own name from mondo_closure at depth 0
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_standards.mondo_closure mc_root
    ON mc_root.descendant_code = cr.concept_id
   AND mc_root.ancestor_code = cr.concept_id
   AND mc_root.depth = 0
  WHERE mh.CPL_MONDO_ID NOT IN (SELECT descendant_code FROM wrc_v1_excluded)
)
SELECT
  comorbidity_root,
  COUNT(DISTINCT USUBJID) AS participants
FROM mh_with_root
GROUP BY comorbidity_root
ORDER BY participants DESC

## CSL-A Body Weight: Storage, Units, and Governing Rule Version

### 1. Where body weight is stored

Raw body-weight observations live in **`silver_vs`** (the SDTM VS domain), filtered by `VSTESTCD = 'WEIGHT'`. The derived Week 24 analysis results (one row per participant × endpoint rule version) are in **`gold_endpoint_result`**, which carries the baseline weight (`BASE`), follow-up weight (`AVAL_FU`), and percent change (`PCHG`). [eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study.gold_endpoint_result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/clinical_study/gold_endpoint_result?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### 2. Analysis-value unit

All analysis values are in **kilograms (kg)**. [Unit normalization (body weight)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/2a363ebb-4203-4002-81ad-8e8fcff7555d?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

- In `silver_vs`, the standardized numeric result `VSSTRESN` is always kg (LB × 0.45359237; g × 0.001). The allowed raw units (`VSORRESU`) are LB, g, and kg; any other raw unit is flagged `UNMAPPED_RAW_UNIT` and excluded from the endpoint.
- In `gold_endpoint_result`, `BASE` and `AVAL_FU` are both in kg; `PCHG` is the unrounded percent change: 100 × (AVAL\_FU − BASE) / BASE. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-f0e6805a-69a8-4a0c-a932-d3505bae2733) [Endpoint definitions (Week 24 weight change)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/81946aa1-f832-4edd-a734-c373cddba9a3?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

Both rule versions are present in the result data (R1 has 3,350 derived results; R2 has 3,525), but per the study's reporting rules, results must never be pooled across rule versions. ## CSL-A-103-0137: Excluded From the Per-Protocol Set Due to a History of Acute Pancreatitis

Participant **CSL-A-103-0137** was excluded from the CSL-A per-protocol set (PPS) because of a **major eligibility violation** — specifically, a medical history of **acute pancreatitis**, which triggered the exclusion criterion **EXC-MH** ("History of an exclusionary condition"). [Clinical Study Lab — Study Analytics (ect)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/genie/rooms/01f1e12bae801258850ed21912b26813?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-6478c9bd-1674-4de3-98dd-5f51fa32ff7f)

### Population Flags

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **FASFL** | Y | In the Full Analysis Set (randomized and dosed) |
| **PPSFL** | N | **Excluded** from the Per-Protocol Set |
| **Reconciliation** | ENROLLED_BUT_RULE_INELIGIBLE | Enrolled despite not meeting the eligibility rule |
| **EDC eligible** | Y | Site recorded the participant as eligible in EDC |
| **Rule eligible** | false | Automated rule engine determined ineligibility |

<!-- begin-embedded:query_tc6CmN -->
| USUBJID | STUDYID | ARMCD | SITEID | FASFL | PPSFL | reconciliation | deviations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CSL-A-103-0137 | CSL-A | CSL101 | SITE-103 | Y | N | ENROLLED_BUT_RULE_INELIGIBLE | [{"deviation":"ELIGIBILITY_VIOLATION","path":[],"evidence":"EXC-MH","severity":"MAJOR","drug":null}] |
<!-- end-embedded:query_tc6CmN -->

The participant was randomized to the **CSL101** arm at **SITE-103** under protocol version **2.0** (eligibility rule **ELIG-A-V2**). [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/e7419adc40204f75b0bade2a2337a278?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_5f8cf3)

### Criterion-Level Traceability

The eligibility engine evaluated all five CSL-A criteria for this participant: [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/e7419adc40204f75b0bade2a2337a278?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_9bc1f5)

| Criterion | Type | Outcome | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| INC-AGE | Inclusion | MET | age = 40 |
| INC-BMI | Inclusion | MET | BMI 39.83 ≥ 30 |
| **EXC-MH** | **Exclusion** | **TRIGGERED** | **acute pancreatitis is\_a\* pancreatitis** |
| EXC-CI | Exclusion | NOT_TRIGGERED | — |
| EXC-CM | Exclusion | NOT_TRIGGERED | — |

The failing criterion was **EXC-MH**: the participant's medical history record (`EDC-MH-CSL-A-103-0137-1`) documented **acute pancreatitis** (MONDO:0006515), which subsumes to **pancreatitis** (MONDO:0004982) via the ontology closure — a condition on the exclusionary medical-history list (class `EXCL-MH-V1`). [Clinical Study Lab — Protocol Evidence (ect)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/genie/rooms/01f1e12bae6816ea9dfd855351a858ff?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### Why the Discrepancy?

The site recorded the participant as eligible in EDC (`edc_eligible = Y`), but the rule-based eligibility engine flagged them as ineligible (`rule_eligible = false`). This **ENROLLED_BUT_RULE_INELIGIBLE** reconciliation status means the participant was enrolled in error — the site missed the exclusionary medical history. Because the PPS excludes all FAS participants with a major protocol deviation, this eligibility violation removed CSL-A-103-0137 from the per-protocol set. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-67638385-4c7a-4e23-909e-0728bf7c0d4d) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-b3040256-583a-41a0-9079-e2c488b7f297)

## SITE-118's Week 24 Visits Were Late Due to Systematic Scheduling Delays at a High-Enrolling Site

The protocol amendment document (CSL-A-PROT-AMD1 §1) provides the definitive explanation: **Week 24 visits at a high-enrolling site were often scheduled 8 to 13 days late**, identified during routine site monitoring in September 2025. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/266351efbab646218cf29e44650d5b5c?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_d03700) This left otherwise complete participants without an evaluable endpoint under the original ±7-day analysis window (EP-A-WT24.R1). [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-72186c3e-544f-4381-a52c-dbb4d27b3832)

### No Monitoring Visit Reports Exist in This System

The document library contains only **PROTOCOL, AMENDMENT, SAP, NOTE, and SPEC** document types — no monitoring visit reports (MVRs) or site-level operational records. [Clinical Study Lab — Protocol Evidence (ect)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/genie/rooms/01f1e12bae6816ea9dfd855351a858ff?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) The closest source is the **Amendment 1 rationale** in CSL-A-PROT-AMD1 §1, which references the monitoring finding without reproducing the MVR itself.

### Scale of the Problem at SITE-118

Of **140 participants** at SITE-118 with a labeled WEEK 24 visit, **98 (70%)** had their visit fall outside the original ±7-day window — all running **+8 to +13 days late**. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/266351efbab646218cf29e44650d5b5c?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_27ad63) Only 42 participants had on-time visits (within ±4 days of target).

<!-- begin-embedded:query_27ad63 -->
| visit_timing | participants | min_days | max_days | avg_days |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Late (>7 days) | 98 | 8 | 13 | 10.6 |
| On time (±7 days) | 42 | -4 | 4 | 0.4 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_27ad63 -->

### Distribution of Late Visits

The lateness was tightly clustered, consistent with a site-level scheduling pattern rather than individual participant issues: [Clinical Study Lab — Study Analytics (ect)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/genie/rooms/01f1e12bae801258850ed21912b26813?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

| Days Late | Participants |
|---|---|
| +8 | 15 |
| +9 | 13 |
| +10 | 16 |
| +11 | 22 |
| +12 | 15 |
| +13 | 17 |

### How Amendment 1 Resolved It

Amendment 1 (protocol 2.0, effective 2025-10-27) widened the Week 24 analysis window from **±7 to ±14 days** (CSL-A-SAP-v2.0 §9.4.1), specifically to recover these participants. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-8cf7d79a-9162-4dd7-95b2-1cd395a59ccf) Under the amended rule (EP-A-WT24.R2), all **98 previously non-evaluable participants** became derivable — their Week 24 observations, which had been excluded as `OUTSIDE_FOLLOWUP_WINDOW` under R1, were selected as `FOLLOWUP_CLOSEST_TO_TARGET` under R2. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-e14628c5-7a89-40dd-9447-1fbaad365514)

### Key Takeaway

The amendment rationale explicitly attributes the late visits to a **scheduling pattern at a high-enrolling site** caught during routine monitoring. The data confirms SITE-118 is that site: it accounts for the vast majority of participants recovered by Amendment 1, with a distinctive +8 to +13 day lateness band that matches the amendment's stated finding. [Baseline and visit-window rules](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/5234158c-899d-46f6-ba1d-98e51d9532ec?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

*Synthetic data — not submission-ready and not for clinical use.*

-- Summary: SITE-118 participants by whether their Week 24 visit was late (>7 days from target) under R1
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN ec.days_from_target > 7 THEN 'Late (>7 days)'
    WHEN ec.days_from_target BETWEEN -7 AND 7 THEN 'On time (±7 days)'
    ELSE 'Other'
  END AS visit_timing,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ec.USUBJID) AS participants,
  MIN(ec.days_from_target) AS min_days,
  MAX(ec.days_from_target) AS max_days,
  ROUND(AVG(ec.days_from_target), 1) AS avg_days
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`gold_endpoint_candidate` ec
JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`clinical_study`.`gold_participant_population` pp
  ON ec.USUBJID = pp.USUBJID
WHERE pp.SITEID = 'SITE-118'
  AND ec.role = 'FOLLOWUP'
  AND ec.rule_version = 'R1'
  AND ec.visit = 'WEEK 24'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
